name: LingBot-Depth
plain: LingBot-Depth (Robbyant, 2026): metric depth completion from an image plus an incomplete or noisy metric depth map (RGB-D camera, LiDAR), and a depth-completion variant (dc). Apache-2.0 code and weights.
summary: LingBot-Depth (Robbyant, 2026): metric depth completion from an image and an incomplete or noisy metric depth map (RGB-D); a DINOv2 ViT-L that attends over image and depth tokens, with MoGe's conv neck and depth / mask heads.

papers.title: Masked Depth Modeling for Spatial Perception

limitations: The depth map is required: call the model with `prompt_depth=` a metric map in metres (any size, holes as 0 / NaN / inf). Its holes change the ViT's token count, so the kernels mode runs the ViT per image. Export keeps every depth token (masked) and has a fixed size.
task_io: Input: one RGB image. Output: a depth or inverse-depth map. `kind` (a card field, `result.kind`) says what the numbers mean: `metric` = metres; `scale_invariant`, `affine_invariant` and `affine_invariant_inverse` are relative (unknown scale or shift, not metres). Metric models that use the focal length take `model(image, intrinsics=K)` (K `[3, 3]`, pixels of the input): `metric3d-vit-large` and `da3metric-large` need it for correct metres (`da3metric-large`: metres = output x focal / 300; without `intrinsics=` a 300 px focal length is assumed, wrong for a real camera). `unidepth-v2-vitl14`, `unik3d-vitl`, `depth-pro` and MoGe estimate the camera themselves (given `intrinsics=` replace `fx`); `zoedepth-nk` and the relative models (`da3mono-large` too) take none. Normals-only models (`kind` `none`) return `result.normals` `[B, H, W, 3]` (unit vectors, camera frame: x right, y down, z forward).

parity.text: CPU, float32: max |diff| <= 0.005 vs the original. GPU, float16 (the default), portable and kernels: mean |diff| <= 1.5 % and p99 <= 5 % of the reference's median |value| (absolute error of the output `depth`).
